extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for HFSP Postdoctoral Fellowships (2024), including applicants from biological and non-biological backgrounds
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for applicants to the 3-year HFSP Postdoctoral Fellowships (Long-Term and Cross-Disciplinary), emphasizing frontier-extending, interdisciplinary basic research and international mobility. Includes eligibility definitions and the two-step submission/review procedure (Letter of Intent then full proposal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel, innovative and interdisciplinary basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP supports novel, innovative and interdisciplinary basic research focused on the complex mechanisms of living organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear emphasis is placed on novel collaborations that bring biologists together to focus on problems at the frontier of the life sciences. Projects should apply novel and interdisciplinary approaches to understand fundamental biological problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frontier-extending and potentially transformative research
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis is placed on whether the research proposal is truly at the frontier of the life sciences and is potentially transformative in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are expected to change scientific paradigms by proposing a frontier-extending research project. Proposals should aim to bring new perspectives to the frontiers of the life sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: International and laboratory mobility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowships are held in a different laboratory, in a new country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mobility is required so that fellows bring new perspectives via working in a different lab and country; the program supports scientific exchanges across national and disciplinary boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of cross-disciplinary applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-Disciplinary Fellowships are for applicants who hold a doctoral degree from a non-biological discipline (e.g. physics, chemistry, mathematics, engineering, or computer sciences) and who have not worked in the life sciences before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program encourages postdocs from outside biology to bring their skills to bear on a fundamental biological problem; such applicants are expected to change research direction into life-science questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Long-Term Fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-Term Fellowships are for applicants with a Ph.D. on a biological topic who want to embark on a novel and frontier project focusing on the life sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure their doctorate is in a biological topic if applying to this track and that their proposed work is novel and frontier-extending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of research direction; no preliminary results expected
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the requirement to change the research direction, no preliminary results are expected when applicants propose their research ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants proposing to move into a new area should not be disadvantaged by lack of preliminary data; proposals are evaluated on frontier potential and novelty rather than existing preliminary results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step application and peer review process (LOI then full proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one competition per year and it follows a two-step application procedure: First, a short Letter of Intent is submitted, which will be peer-reviewed by an HFSP review committee. The best Letters of Intent are then invited to submit a full proposal, which will again be peer-reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a concise LOI via the online platform (https://proposalcentral.com) in the stated submission window; only competitive LOIs will be invited to the full proposal stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of Intent: short and competitive
rubrics_metrics.description: First, a short Letter of Intent is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The LOI should be concise and focused on the frontier/transformative aspects of the project because it is the first, peer-reviewed gate for invitation to submit a full proposal. Submission deadlines and platform details are provided on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation of application guidelines and confirmation of eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying, please read carefully the HFSP website as well as the application guidelines which list the eligibility criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear about eligibility, applicants should contact the fellowship office at fellow@hfsp.org. The application guidelines contain full eligibility rules and other procedural requirements beyond the high-level criteria on this page.
